key_insight: Magic state injections enable universal transversal quantum circuits while keeping sequential decoding volumes statistically bounded in the random circuits studied.
engineering_relevance: Sequentially decoding measurements and committing corrections could make space-time correlated decoding practical for large fault-tolerant quantum computations.
method: Backpropagate logical measurement operators to construct space-time decoding graphs.
Decode measurements sequentially, commit corrections, and exclude previously processed syndrome data.
Compare decoding volumes across injection densities, measurement products, circuit connectivities, and Clifford gate ensembles.
evidence_signal: In random circuits, mid-circuit decoding volumes approach a stationary average set by magic state injection density, with exponentially suppressed large instances and similar qualitative behavior across tested circuit variations.
watch_item: The abstract establishes decoding-volume behavior in random circuits, not end-to-end decoder runtime or performance on structured quantum algorithms.
paper_title: Bounded decoding complexity in transversal circuits with magic state injection
